title: Start a shift, collect the wards, end the shift
journey: The driver binds the phone to a van, starts the shift (trip snapshot taken), marks each ward collected, and ends the shift; the trip record is the evidence the office later reads.

steps.action: The driver enters the driver code (AB-1234), the app reads drivers/{CODE} and shows the confirm card (driver name, allotted van, ward count, masked phone); the code is remembered on-device for returning drivers.
steps.notes: The bind (vanDevices/{vanId}) would be done by bindDeviceToVan, but the driver app reads drivers/{CODE} directly instead; no callable is called.

steps.action: Start Shift creates the trips doc (vanId, routeId from the van, driverId, wardIds snapshot from the driver, date = IST midnight, startedAt) and sets vans.status = on_shift and vans.currentTripId = tripId, atomically on the van doc.
steps.notes: The wardIds snapshot is taken at shift start so a mid-shift allotment change does not rewrite today's record. currentTripId is the atomic marker.

steps.action: The driver marks each ward done; mark_ward_done_flow appends {wardId, doneAt, flagged} to trips.wardsDone of today's open trip (out-of-order marks allowed, flagged when outside the ward radius).
steps.notes: Direct Firestore write through TripsRepository.appendWardDone; not a callable. The ward must be in the trip's wardIds snapshot.

steps.action: End Shift sets trips.endedAt, vans.status = idle, and vans.currentTripId = null, then stops tracking and flushes the GPS trail.
steps.notes: Shared write set (end_shift_writes.dart) also used by the depot auto-end rule (ruling #29).

slices.evidence: lib/features/shift_start/domain/start_shift.dart creates the trip and sets vans.currentTripId + status = on_shift via repositories; lib/features/live_route/mark_ward_done_flow.dart appends wardsDone; lib/core/domain/end_shift_writes.dart ends the shift. All are direct Firestore writes, not callables.
04-functions/src/callables/shift.ts and identity.ts contain real callable code, but callables.json marks all four lifecycle as planned.
slices.blockedBy: No app calls these callables; the driver app writes trips and vans directly to Firestore instead. bindDeviceToVan, startShift, endShift and markWardDone are unused.

handoffs.notes: The driver's shift writes are the trip record the office reads later; no callable mediates them.

scenario.name: Shift start, ward collection, end shift (PRD-2 driver feature)
steps: Driver enters the code and confirms the allotted van and ward count.
Driver taps Start Shift; the trip doc is created and vans.currentTripId is set.
Driver marks each ward done; trips.wardsDone grows.
Driver ends the shift; trips.endedAt is set and vans.currentTripId is cleared.
Killing and reopening the app mid-shift resumes the open trip without re-entering the code.

openQuestions: The driver app writes trips and vans directly instead of calling startShift / endShift / markWardDone; decide whether to wire the callables or keep direct writes as the canonical path.
bindDeviceToVan is specified but never called; the driver app reads drivers/{CODE} directly. Confirm whether the device-to-van binding is ever created.
The user app's stack is React/Vite, not Flutter as the PRD states.
